title: FTL vs PTL: Which Is Right for Your Business?
excerpt: Choosing between full truck load and part truck load can cut your logistics cost significantly. Here is a simple guide for Indian shippers.
content:
When you need to move goods across India, one of the first decisions is whether you need a full truck load (FTL) or a part truck load (PTL).

Full truck load is ideal when your cargo fills most of the vehicle. You get a dedicated truck, faster transit, fewer handling points, and better control over the schedule.

Part truck load is cost-effective when your shipment is smaller. You share space with other consignments and pay mainly for the volume or weight you use.

At SHYAM LOGISTIC, we help you compare both options for your route, cargo type, and delivery timeline—so you never overpay for empty truck space.

Tips to decide:
- Choose FTL if cargo is urgent, high-value, or near full capacity
- Choose PTL if your load is partial and cost savings matter more than an exclusive vehicle
- Share exact weight, dimensions, and origin–destination cities for a clear quote

title: How to Prepare Cargo for Safe Road Transport
excerpt: Proper packing and documents reduce damage risk and transit delays. Use this checklist before your next booking.
content:
Safe road transport starts before the truck arrives. Good preparation protects your goods and keeps delivery on schedule.

1) Pack for the road
Use sturdy packaging, edge protectors for heavy materials, and moisture barriers where needed. Label fragile packages clearly.

2) Share accurate details
Weight, dimensions, pickup access, and special handling notes help the transporter choose the right vehicle.

3) Keep documents ready
Invoice, packing list, e-way bill (where applicable), and GST details should be ready for smooth transit and delivery.

4) Plan pickup and unloading
Confirm a contact person, site access hours, and unloading equipment if the cargo is heavy.

title: Pan-India Freight Tips for Small Businesses
excerpt: Small and mid-sized businesses can keep freight reliable without a large fleet. Follow these practical steps.
content:
You do not need your own fleet to run pan-India deliveries. The right logistics partner and a simple process can do most of the work.

Start with standard routes
If you ship regularly on the same lanes, share that pattern with your transporter. Fixed routes often get better planning and rates.

Use part load wisely
PTL is often enough for retail and B2B stock movement. Book early for festival or month-end peak times.

Track through one contact
Keep one booking reference and one coordinator so status checks are fast.

Ask for GST billing
Transparent invoices help with accounting and trust.
